rust_authorities: Rust now owns canonical player/alias schema migration, capacity and serialized allocation, canonical account and couch-seat/party lookups, provider-name/profile updates, stable registration metadata and public friend-tag assignment. The complete dual-provider adoption transaction is Rust-owned: raw Steam bearer/current SQL expiry checks before and after Discord provider IO; current canonical aliases, one-provider uniqueness, all declared persistent player foreign-key checks with paged schema enumeration and quoted identifiers; actual native primary/signed-local session checks; atomic metadata-only adoption; persisted registration clock floor; and sealed post-COMMIT revocation of the deleted player's native account grants. Caller-owned canonical transactions and failed composed writes preserve the caller's earlier writes through typed SQLite savepoints; link operations reject outer transactions before provider IO. Three real controls go red before the port: canonical resolution commits its caller transaction, and links succeed after primary expiry or revocation during provider await. A subsequent native commit-effect regression exposed and fixed consumption of the shared readiness flag; failed COMMIT preserves the old mapping/grants and a successful retry retires the old grant. Python retains generic provider/source admission, HTTP/clock/SQLite IO and temporary endpoint coordination. Steam OpenID verification/pending/session/refresh issuance, Discord verifier policy, full Rust service/middleware replacement, cross-store/process recovery and all original/native played/delivered gates remain open. These are modern identity service rules, not recovered Xbox Live authentication. Rust also resolves complete couch rosters atomically: the reproduced one-free-slot/two-new-seats503 previously retained the first canonical player/profile/alias/tag; the final Rust roster transaction rolls all four tables back and publishes no native session. Successful primary/signed-local allocation uses distinct native identities and never stores a guest account.
